33.title: A stranger rings your mother's doorbell.
paragraphs: She lives far from you. Another city, or another country. The bags got heavy this year. She needs more time on the stairs.
So there is an ad online. Someone answered it the same day. You do not know their name or their past. No one you know has met them.
She lets them in. The bags are heavy.
A stranger is inside your mother's home. The ad site asked for a phone number and nothing more.
Help came in one day. No one could check the stranger.
33.alt: A plain parchment card with dark serif text, no photo. The text tells a short story. Your mother lets in a stranger who answered her ad. There is no way to know who they are.

34.title: You call your father on Sunday.
paragraphs: He says all is fine. He means it as a kindness. He does not want you to worry.
So you hear none of it. The fridge is down to milk and little else. The mail sits unopened by the door. He moved his bed downstairs, because of the stairs.
More children than ever live in a different city from their parents. Often a different country.
From that far, you know what he chooses to tell you. His voice sounds fine. The house around him is a guess.
A call cannot show you the fridge, the mail or the stairs.
34.alt: A calm parchment card with dark serif text. It describes a phone call to a father who lives alone. He says all is fine. The card lists what the caller cannot see. The fridge is near empty. The mail is unopened. He stays off the stairs.

35.title: Picture a quiet week at your mother's place.
paragraphs: Monday, the groceries come to the door. Tuesday, the pension lands in the bank. The TV works. The pills arrive on time. Nothing breaks.
She has everything she needs. Nobody comes to the door all week.
Quiet like that harms the body. The US Surgeon General compares chronic loneliness to smoking 15 cigarettes a day.
Sunday evening comes. The kettle boils for one. Next week looks the same.
35.alt: A pale card with dark text. One line for each day of the week. Groceries arrive, the pension arrives, the TV works, the pills come, nothing breaks. The Sunday line says nobody came. A last line says the week before went the same way.

36.title: Your mother pays online now.
paragraphs: Groceries from her chair. The gas bill from bed. A birthday gift from the kitchen table.
Ten years ago she handed cash over a counter. Now the shop is inside her phone.
She learned all of it late in life. Passwords. One-time codes. She did the work.
Scammers went after elders first. Cybercrime against Indian seniors rose 86% in two years (NCRB, 2020 to 2022).
She deserves to be safe online. No one built protection around her.
36.alt: A plain parchment card with dark serif text, no photo. It says she pays online now. Groceries, the gas bill, a gift for a grandchild. Scammers went after her first. Cybercrime against Indian seniors rose 86% in two years (NCRB, 2020 to 2022). She moved online faster than anyone built protection around her.

37.title: The thing I saw that I think no one else noticed.
paragraphs: My father pays online all the time, from his phone. My grandfather does not. My grandfather is an elder today. My father is an adult today.
Now think ten years ahead. When my father grows old, he will join the first generation of elders who already use phones and pay online, at mass scale. The first in the history of the world.
My father's generation will come to old age already digital. A new kind of user, in a new market. It opened my mind.
I noted it down. The whole idea stands on that one note. Towinly grew out of it.
Harshavardhan Anbu Gowri, founder of Towinly
37.alt: A pale blue card with dark serif text, laid out like a founder's note. The card says his father pays online all the time and his grandfather does not. It says his father will one day join the first generation of elders who already use phones and pay online. A small green tortoise faces right on the first dot of a six-dot track near the bottom, marking part one of six. The card is unsigned.

38.title: I wanted to build something real for old people. First I had to name the problem.
paragraphs: Elders face two problems. Loneliness. And tasks that take energy.
So I started to mix people.
Elders have life lessons, money, advice, and a lot of time. They want company. Someone to move around with. Someone who helps.
Young people like me have energy to spare. And what we need is what elders have. Life lessons. Money. Advice.
Each side holds what the other needs. That is the mix.

But one condition matters most. Helpers must bring the love and care they would give their own grandparents. An elder should never feel the helper is just doing a job. Money is part of it too. Love and care come first.
That is the problem I chose: connecting elders and helpers, on those terms.
It takes two To Win.
Harshavardhan Anbu Gowri, founder of Towinly
38.alt: A pale blue card with dark serif text in the founder's voice. It lists what elders have and what young people have. It states the rule: helpers come with love and care first. A small green tortoise faces right on the second dot of a six-dot track near the bottom, marking part two of six. The card is unsigned.

39.title: How I built trust.
paragraphs: I wanted to connect elders with helpers they had never met. The biggest problem with that is trust. Scammers go after elders. Elders deserve to be safe.

So I asked myself: how did I come to trust my own friend? Day one, I knew him and nothing more. His hobbies came later. The deeper things came much later. Full trust took a long time. It came in layers.
So Towinly climbs the same seven layers, and both people say yes to every step:
1. Just Connected
2. Messaging
3. Phone Ready
4. Video Ready
5. Social Media
6. Ready to Meet
7. Fully Trusted
Nothing personal, like a phone number, is shared until trust has grown.
That is the Trust Ladder. The next part is the other half: the Trust Score.
Trust between people is slow. Slow is the point.
Harshavardhan Anbu Gowri, founder of Towinly
39.alt: A pale blue card titled How I built trust. Serif text tells how trust in a friend arrived in layers over a long journey, and says Towinly climbs the same seven layers. A ladder list names all seven steps: Just Connected, Messaging, Phone Ready, Video Ready, Social Media, Ready to Meet, Fully Trusted, the last one in gold. Below it says both people say yes to every step and nothing personal, like a phone number, is shared until trust has grown. A small green tortoise faces right on the third dot of a six-dot track, marking part three of six. The card is unsigned.

40.title: One day I asked myself: what if I die? An accident, something out of nowhere. I hope it never happens. But what if it does?
paragraphs: I have ideas in my head that no one knows about. Things I need the world to know.
And there are things I want to tell my mother. Things I want to tell my father. I keep putting it off. I tell myself: next year. Once I get somewhere.
Then the question comes back. What if something bad happens first?
So Towinly keeps three boxes: for the ideas, for the secrets, for everything I do not want to lose.
The Stories box. How you met, what you learned the hard way, the ideas you want the world to know, the recipe nobody else has.
The Letters box. A letter goes to one person, and only that person. It can be read today, or held until after you are gone.
The Sealed box. Your secrets. The things only you know. Where the money is. Which bank. Where the papers are kept. It opens only after you are gone.

Nothing opens on its own. Before anything held is passed on, a person at Towinly checks a death certificate, asks the people you chose, and tries to reach you for thirty days. And you choose who sees each one.
For elders this matters more. They are in the last stage of life. They have more, and they know more about life.
That question is where the boxes came from.
Harshavardhan Anbu Gowri, founder of Towinly
40.alt: A pale blue card titled Where the boxes came from. In calm serif text the founder asks what if I die, an accident, something out of nowhere. He says he has ideas no one knows about and things he keeps meaning to tell his mother and his father. Three white boxes are named Stories box, Letters box, and Sealed box, each with a line on what it keeps. The Stories box holds the ideas you want the world to know, the Sealed box opens with the words your secrets and says it opens only after you are gone. A small green tortoise faces right on the fifth dot of a six-dot track, marking part five of six. The card is unsigned.

41.title: As a child I wanted to be a scientist.
paragraphs: Later I found the real wish. I wanted to build an app for old people. One that solves a real problem they face. Every idea I had needed the same thing: people. A community.
A few years ago, an app like this took a big team. I knew that. I was one person.
Now there is AI.

I am a computer science master's student in Montreal. I am a software developer. So one person can do the whole job today. I build the app. I test it. I run the database. I write these posts. I learn the rest from the internet.
I could not have done this alone before. Now I can, and that is new.
I carried this wish for years. So here I am, building Towinly.
Harshavardhan Anbu Gowri
Founder of Towinly
41.alt: A calm pale blue card titled One person is building Towinly. The founder says a few years ago this took a big team and now there is AI. A white card lists his jobs: the app, the tests, the database, the posts, the rest learned from the internet. Signed in serif italics Harshavardhan Anbu Gowri, founder of Towinly, the only signed card in the six-part series. The green tortoise faces right and reaches the last dot of the six-dot track.

42.title: Trust comes from belief. And belief comes from evidence and pattern.
paragraphs: A pattern needs repetition. I cannot trust what someone says once. I can trust what someone does, again and again.
Think of a bus driver, or a pilot. You have never met them, and you still step aboard. Their training and their certificates are the evidence. Every safe trip before yours is the pattern.
Towinly builds the same two things. Evidence: ID proof, certificates, social profiles, reviews. Repetition and pattern: connection after connection, each one adding to the record.

That is the Trust Score. A checked profile is worth 3 points. The seven steps of the Trust Ladder are worth 7. Reviews are worth 5. Each person you connect with can add up to 15 points. The score is a reputation. It keeps changing as you connect with new people.
Trust between people is slow. Slow is the point.
Harshavardhan Anbu Gowri, founder of Towinly

Two white cards name Evidence (ID proof, certificates, social profiles, reviews) and Repetition / Pattern (connection after connection, each one adding to the record). Serif text says the founder already trusts a bus driver or a pilot he has never met: their training and certificates are the evidence, every safe trip before his is the pattern. 47.title: Five people. A switch for each friendship.
paragraphs: An elder can invite up to five family members to stay close and step in if they are ever needed.
They see the journey: each friendship climbing its seven steps. They hear right away: alerts the moment something needs attention. They help decide: look at a new helper and share their view.
The elder is always in charge. Every friendship has its own switch, on or off, at any time.
47.alt: A warm cream card titled Five people. A switch for each friendship. A row of five small circles sits under the title. Three white cards read See the journey, watch each friendship climb its seven steps; Hear right away, alerts the moment something needs attention; Help decide, look at a new helper and share their view. A drawn switch in the on position sits beside the line The elder is always in charge. Every friendship has its own switch, on or off, at any time. The foot reads It takes two To Win. and towinly.trust.

02.title: On Towinly, trust is a ladder you climb together.
paragraphs: Seven steps from "Just Connected" to "Fully Trusted." Both people say yes to every step, and personal details stay private until you're both ready.
Slow and steady. That's the whole idea.
02.alt: Labelled "The Trust Ladder". Headline: "Seven steps. Both of you say yes to every one." A numbered rail runs down the page through seven rungs, the first three filled in blue and the last marked with a tortoise, each naming a step and what it does: 1 Just Connected, see each other's profile and send a connection request; 2 Messaging, send messages and share photos in a private chat; 3 Phone Ready, share phone numbers and call each other, and nothing before this step shows a number; 4 Video Ready, have a video call and meet face to face; 5 Social Media, both share their Instagram, Facebook or other profiles; 6 Ready to Meet, plan to meet in person and emergency contacts are told; 7 Fully Trusted, a full trusted friendship with reviews both ways. Below: "Either of you can pause or stop at any time. Every step is worth one point of the trust score, and there is no rush at any of them."
